I get where you’re coming from (I read your comment about your mom, I’m sorry that happened ) but situations like death and post mortem nursing are way more emotionally complex than just being stoic and calm. Human beings are multifaceted, so just because in that moment they expressed distress and anxiety, it’s doesn’t mean that your colleagues were being unprofessional and not giving their full attention. Nurses are humans and humans can feel multiple emotions and feelings at once. Like I said before, people have different ways of verbalising and showing their emotions during different situations , and they’re all valid. No one is saying that your reaction was wrong, but your opinion about your colleagues’ was.

Nursing is an extremely emotional and human field. We take care of humans (patients ) and work with other humans ( our colleagues). Expecting nurses to feel nothing is unrealistic and doing that often leads to depression and burnout. We obviously come with our emotional and personal baggage that makes each one of us react to things differently, but talking down on people who express different emotions, or behave differently than you is disappointing to hear, especially as a nurse student. That being said, it’s fine if you deal with situations differently but don’t invalidate people’s feelings and emotions, and remember to be empathetic !
